objectives: Recognize recurring rime patterns in /k/ CVC words.
Use onset-rime awareness without replacing phoneme decoding.
Read controlled sentences containing /k/ CVC words.
concepts: Word families share a recurring rime.
Onset-rime supports efficient recognition after phoneme knowledge is secure.
Connected reading requires accurate decoding and meaning checks.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing a common ending pattern and rime.
The initial consonant sound or consonant cluster before the rime.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.

workedExamples: cat, cap, can show related CVC patterns but each must still be decoded accurately.
The /k/ onset can combine with -at, -it, -op, or -ub to form different words.
commonMistakes: Reading a family pattern without checking the onset.
Reading isolated words correctly but losing accuracy in sentences.
keyTakeaways: Use the pattern in connected text.

basic: Read /k/ CVC words grouped by family.
conceptual: Identify onset and rime in simple words.
application: Read patterned words in controlled sentences.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how word-family recognition can support speed without encouraging guessing.
mixedReview: Combine /k/ decoding, word families, and controlled sentence reading.

quickRevision: identify onset → identify rime → blend → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If a family word is guessed, return to each phoneme and blend.
weakTopicRevision: Practice the family with new onset or final-sound contrasts while preserving accurate decoding.

activities.name: Onset swap
steps: Change the final consonant where appropriate.

outcomes: Learner recognizes common /k/ CVC word-family patterns.
Learner applies word-family knowledge in controlled sentences.
Learner maintains decoding accuracy during connected reading.
